video_title: Jalen Duren Actually Wants Sacramento? Marc Spears Drops New Details

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Scott Perry's deep ties to Jalen Duren and the Pistons
quotes.excerpt: Scott Perry has a relationship with Jalen Duren dating to when he was trying to get the Knicks
quotes.quote: Scott Perry is not playing around, neither is BJ Armstrong. Scott Perry has a relationship with Jalen Duren dating to when he was trying to get the Knicks to draft him, which they did, but they traded him to the Pistons. Scott Perry also has NFL ties from his father. Duren's agent is an NFL agent, so he has a connection with him. Duren likes Scott Perry a lot. He likes Sacramento a lot, but the Pistons, their focus on bringing him back, they have some optimism, but it is complicated.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Scott Perry's relationship with Jalen Duren goes beyond off-season meetings
quotes.excerpt: Scott Perry's relationship with Jalen Duren goes beyond a dinner meeting or a conversation
quotes.quote: Scott Perry's relationship with Jalen Duren goes beyond a dinner meeting or a conversation that they had earlier in the off-season when Scott was at least wooing Duren or at least having a conversation with Duren about what we would envision you being a part of the Sacramento Kings if you would want to sign here. That is not where the conversation started. They knew each other from before that. Obviously, you heard the family ties with Duren's dad being an NFL agent. So, it is very interesting to me to hear an extra added layer that supports the growing belief or confidence that Duren wanting to play in Sacramento is not just because Sacramento is willing to throw the bag, but Duren likes the idea of where the Kings are going, likes who is running the Sacramento Kings in Scott Perry, and likes the idea of being paired with a young guard in Darius A. Cuff Jr.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Dismissing the narrative that Sacramento is a 'cowtown dump'
quotes.excerpt: It is not a joke, and to say such things is just arrogant and disrespectful
quotes.quote: It is not a joke, and to say such things is just arrogant and disrespectful from this elitist mindset that Sacramento is a cowtown dump. This reputation that has been constantly disproven over the years that the Kings have existed here in Sacramento. Players have maybe not wanted to come here in the past, but once they are here, it is different for them. There have not been instances for a very long time that players have come to Sacramento and gone, 'I hate it here, it sucks here, this place is horrible.' You never hear that, you never see that, because that is not the case.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Pascal Siakam's failed deal with the Kings was about money
quotes.excerpt: Pascal Siakam was going to be a King. It was done. Siakam was excited about it
quotes.quote: Pascal Siakam was going to be a King. It was done. Siakam was excited about it. The deal fell apart because the Kings refused to pay him. That is not because Pascal Siakam did not want to play in Sacramento. So, I think this archaic, insulting mindset that these players wouldn't want to play for the Sacramento Kings because they don't want to play in Sacramento is foolish, and it is ridiculous, especially from people who call Sacramento home. It is not true.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's contract options and the October 1st deadline
quotes.excerpt: He could basically take the one-year $9.6 million qualifying offer. Keep an eye on October 1st
quotes.quote: He could basically take the one-year $9.6 million qualifying offer. Keep an eye on October 1st, that is the deadline when he has until to sign that. Or he can sign this lucrative contract that is going to pay him $35 to $36 million and go back to Detroit on a long-term contract here. It hasn't been done before on a player like his level besides Greg Monroe, and that is dating back. It worked out for Greg Monroe because he signed a three-year max the following year with Milwaukee.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Contract negotiations for max players like Kentavious Caldwell-Pope
quotes.excerpt: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is a max player. Every penny we can give, there is not going to be a contract negotiation
quotes.quote: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is a max player. Every penny we can give, there is not going to be a contract negotiation with Victor Wembanyama. When Wembanyama is up for, or did he already get his? He did it and he took a pay cut. So, credit to Wembanyama. Maybe that is a bad example, but some of these max contract players are, if this is what you want, we will give it to you. That is players that elevate to that level in the NBA. There isn't a conversation, so there isn't any friction.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Simmons' health and role with the Kings
quotes.excerpt: He is healthy, he took a year off to get healthy, and they list him at guard
quotes.quote: He is healthy, he took a year off to get healthy, and they list him at guard. They want him to back up Darius A. Cuff Jr. and he is already in Sacramento getting ready for next season.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on Ben Simmons' talent and health
quotes.excerpt: I'm happy to see Ben Simmons back in the NBA. Ben Simmons is a talent that doesn't grow
quotes.quote: I'm happy to see Ben Simmons back in the NBA. Ben Simmons is a talent that doesn't grow on trees and we don't get the opportunity to see in the NBA every day. Got off to a very promising start in his career and then a lot of people tried to blame his game and not his injuries. I actually had a conversation with Ben Simmons. First thing he says is, 'Man, I'm healthy.' It feels so good to be healthy.

quotes.speaker: Matt
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Simmons' potential impact on Darius A. Cuff Jr.
quotes.excerpt: This will take some of the pressure off Darius A. Cuff. If Ben Simmons isn't playing well
quotes.quote: This will take some of the pressure off Darius A. Cuff. If Ben Simmons isn't playing well, people are going to want to point to Ben Simmons and say, 'Hey, he's not playing well.' And if he is playing well, people are going to point to Ben Simmons and say, 'Yo, look, he's back.' And so I think this ultimately takes a lot of pressure off Darius A. Cuff, going into a Sacramento Kings situation that is not as great as one would like for a general manager who knows as much as Scott Perry does. I think that's one of the decided factors, if not the decided factor behind this move.
